recipes.notes: One 30 g scoop of a generic whey powder blended with whole milk, one banana and frozen berries. BLS lists the berry mix raw; freezing does not change its nutrients. Oat drink (bls:C660000) is the usual swap and is left to editing.

One home-made 30 cm pizza: BLS raw pizza dough, passata, one 125 g ball of mozzarella, a few basil leaves and a spoon of olive oil. Water lost from the dough while baking is not modelled, as in the café recipes. USDA mozzarella is used because the BLS rows leave fibre undeclared, which would drop fibre from the whole dish.
About 100 g of dry spaghetti cooked to 250 g, with BLS's own beef bolognese sauce and a spoon of grated parmesan. The parmesan is optional but included in the default serving.
50 g oat flakes cooked in 200 g whole milk with a small grated apple. No sugar or cinnamon; cinnamon's table row leaves iodine undeclared and adds almost nothing.
60 g unsweetened muesli with dried fruit over 150 g plain 3.5 % yoghurt. Sweetened crunchy muesli is a different food and stays a separate search.
Two large eggs (60 g each without shell), a splash of milk and a knob of butter for the pan. The serving counts eggs, so "three scrambled eggs" is one and a half servings.

Three small American pancakes from flour, milk, half an egg and butter for batter and pan. Baking powder and sugar are left out: their BLS rows leave saturated fat, water and other values undeclared, which would remove them from the whole dish. Syrup is logged separately.
Two 40 g slices of wheat-rye bread with half a large avocado, a squeeze of lemon and a drizzle of olive oil. The serving counts slices.
A main-course chicken caesar: romaine, one grilled marinated chicken breast, shaved parmesan, croutons and two tablespoons of regular caesar dressing.
Tomato, cucumber, onion and green pepper with a 60 g slice of feta, a few olives and a tablespoon of olive oil. USDA feta is used because the BLS feta leaves fibre undeclared.

A restaurant-style bowl made at home: rice, canned black beans, grilled chicken, sweetcorn, red salsa, lettuce, cheddar, sour cream and guacamole. It is a large serving on purpose; most people's bowls are.

A coconut chicken curry over 180 g cooked rice: braised chicken breast, coconut milk, onion, passata, curry powder and olive oil. Olive oil stands in for rapeseed or sunflower oil because their BLS rows leave water undeclared, which would drop water from the whole dish. Plain "chicken curry" keeps the USDA dish without rice.
Passata simmered with broth, onion and olive oil, finished with a spoon of cream. The cream is optional but included in the default serving.

Spätzle are fresh egg pasta, so BLS's cooked fresh egg pasta stands in for them, layered with grated Bergkäse, home-fried onions and butter. Emmentaler is the usual swap; its BLS row leaves vitamin C undeclared.
One plate-sized pancake, a fifth of the usual 250 g flour, 500 ml milk and 4 eggs batter, fried in butter. In Berlin a Pfannkuchen is a doughnut; that BLS row stays reachable by search.

The southern German style with broth, onion, vinegar and oil rather than mayonnaise, as a main-course side. The oil is olive oil for the same water-coverage reason as the curry. A mayonnaise salad is noticeably richer and is left to editing.

A vegetarian German lentil stew: cooked lentils, potato, carrot, celeriac and onion in broth with a dash of vinegar and olive oil. USDA lentils are used because the BLS cooked lentils leave sodium undeclared. Sausages are common but not universal and are left to adding.
50 g oat flakes soaked overnight in milk and yoghurt, topped with blueberries. Chia is a common extra; its BLS row leaves vitamin C undeclared.
A plain three-egg omelette with a splash of milk, cooked in butter. Fillings are added as their own ingredients.

A frozen banana and berry mix blended with yoghurt, topped with granola and a few strawberries. USDA plain whole-milk yoghurt is used because the BLS yoghurt leaves vitamin C undeclared, which would hide the fruit's vitamin C.
